lines.en: I’m so tired lately, Mina. I can’t sleep well on work nights.
lines.pt: Estou tão cansado ultimamente, Mina. Não consigo dormir bem nas noites de trabalho.

lines.en: Oh no. **What’s going on?** When did it start?
lines.pt: Ai, não. O que está acontecendo? Quando começou?

lines.en: When I started the new job. I check my email until midnight.
lines.pt: Quando comecei o emprego novo. Fico checando e-mail até meia-noite.

lines.en: **You should** stop looking at your phone an hour before bed.
lines.pt: Você deveria parar de olhar o celular uma hora antes de dormir.

lines.en: Maybe, but I’m afraid I’ll miss something important.
lines.pt: Talvez, mas tenho medo de perder algo importante.

lines.en: **Why don’t you** turn off email notifications after nine? Real emergencies come by phone.
lines.pt: Por que você não desliga as notificações de e-mail depois das nove? Emergências de verdade chegam por telefone.

lines.en: That’s a good idea. What else?
lines.pt: É uma boa ideia. O que mais?

lines.en: **If I were you,** I’d talk to my boss about work hours. **And you shouldn’t** drink coffee after four.
lines.pt: Se eu fosse você, conversaria com meu chefe sobre horários. E você não deveria tomar café depois das quatro.

lines.en: You’re right. I’ll try both. Thanks for listening, Mina.
lines.pt: Você tem razão. Vou tentar as duas coisas. Obrigado por me ouvir, Mina.

pages.title: Giving a Friend Friendly Advice

situation.text: A friend tells you about a small problem: he cannot sleep because of his new job. You listen, ask a question and give friendly, useful advice without sounding bossy.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can listen to a problem, ask about it and give friendly advice in different ways — polite and clear.
canDo: Ask about a problem: What’s going on?
Give advice: You should… / You shouldn’t…
Give a personal opinion: If I were you, I’d…
success: I give two pieces of advice.
I react to my friend’s answer.
pages.think: When a friend has a problem, do you give advice right away or listen first? How do you say it in English without sounding bossy?

teach.goal: Abrir a aula pela situação real, não pela regra.
solo: Leia o objetivo e peça que o estudante diga, com as próprias palavras, o que vai conseguir fazer hoje.
Faça a pergunta “Think about it” antes de mostrar qualquer expressão.
group: Cada estudante diz uma palavra ou ideia que associa à situação.
Mostre os critérios de sucesso: eles são a missão final da aula.
support: Aceite respostas curtas ou em português na primeira rodada e reformule em inglês.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.solo: Start with real questions about the student’s life, not a grammar test.
intro.group: One question per student, then a follow-up question to a classmate.

pages.recall: Opinions: “I think… / I’d rather…”. Ask: What do you think is the best way to relax after work?

qs.q: How did you sleep last night?
qs.pt: Como você dormiu ontem à noite?

qs.q: What do you do when you feel stressed?
qs.pt: O que você faz quando está estressado?

qs.q: Who gives you the best advice?
qs.pt: Quem dá os melhores conselhos para você?

pages.tip: Use the answers to find gaps and to recycle earlier content. The goal is to enter English from the first minute.

teach.goal: Entrar no idioma no primeiro minuto e mapear lacunas.
extra: What time do you go to bed?
What is the best advice you ever got?

errors.r: I slept badly. / I didn’t sleep well.

support: Ofereça as respostas-modelo (chips) e peça apenas que escolham uma e a ampliem com um motivo.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Advice among friends
pages.intro: In the USA, friends often ask before they give advice, and they soften it with “maybe” or “if I were you”. Look and guess before you read.

cards.note: Asking first shows respect: some people only want to be heard.
A soft suggestion is less bossy than an order.
People often thank a friend for listening, not only for advice.

qs.q: Why do people ask “Do you want my advice?”
qs.pt: Por que perguntam “Do you want my advice?”

levels.A2: It shows respect for the other person.
levels.B1: Because some people just want to talk, and unrequested advice can feel pushy.
levels.B2: Asking permission respects autonomy, since unsolicited advice may feel critical even when well meant.

qs.q: How can you give advice without sounding bossy?
qs.pt: Como dar conselho sem soar mandão?

levels.A2: Use Why don’t you…? or If I were you…
levels.B1: Use softer forms: Why don’t you…?, Maybe you could…, If I were you, I’d…
levels.B2: Suggestion forms present options rather than orders, which keeps the tone equal between friends.

qs.q: Is “You must…” a good way to give advice?
qs.pt: “You must…” é uma boa forma de aconselhar?

levels.B1: It can sound like an order; should is softer.
levels.B2: Must is strong and is better reserved for rules and urgent situations; should expresses advice more gently.

pages.compare: In Brazil friends often give direct advice right away: “Faz assim.” In the USA people often ask first and soften it. Which feels more natural to you?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto cultural e as primeiras hipóteses.
solo: Mostre os cartões e peça hipóteses antes de explicar.
Peça que compare com o que acontece no Brasil.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica em uma frase.
Pergunte “Do you agree?” entre colegas.
answers: Q1: respeito; às vezes a pessoa só quer ser ouvida.
Q2: Why don’t you / Maybe you could / If I were you.
Q3: must é forte; should é conselho.
extra: Do you like to receive advice?
support: Use as respostas de nível A1 como andaime e peça que repitam.
stretch: B2: compare o registro e o tom entre Brasil e EUA com exemplos reais.

pass1.pt: Qual é o problema do Joe?

teach.goal: Compreender a situação antes de ver o texto: ideia principal e depois informações específicas.
solo: Esconda o texto. 1ª escuta: só a ideia principal.
2ª escuta: peça os detalhes pedidos nas tarefas. Só depois mostre o texto.
group: Escuta coletiva; duplas anotam antes de revelar.
Compare as respostas entre duplas e só então mostre o texto.
answers: Pass 2: new job · email · midnight · boss · coffee
extra: Is Mina bossy or friendly? Why?
support: Pause depois de cada fala se necessário.

opts: When Joe started the new job
Stop looking at the phone before bed

qs.q: Why is Joe afraid to turn off notifications?
What does Joe say at the end?

retell.prompt: Retell the conversation in your own words, at your level.

teach.goal: Ler o diálogo, perceber os chunks e recontar.
solo: O estudante lê um papel e você lê o outro; depois troquem.
Peça que reconte a conversa no nível que conseguir.
group: Leitura em duplas e troca de papéis.
Reconto em cadeia: uma frase por estudante.
answers: When Joe started the new job · Stop looking at the phone before bed · He might miss something important · He will try both ideas
extra: What advice would YOU give Joe?
support: Mostre a tradução (botão PT) depois da 2ª leitura.

pages.title: Useful expressions

items.en: You should stop looking at your phone.
Why don’t you turn off notifications?
If I were you, I’d talk to my boss.

pages.note: Instead of memorizing the whole list, choose 3–5 expressions (★) to use again and again. The others are for understanding and for stretching later.

teach.goal: Escolher 3–5 chunks para uso repetido e descobrir a função de cada um.
solo: Pergunte “When do you say it?” antes de dar o significado.
Compare formal × informal e peça um exemplo próprio.
group: Cada estudante escolhe a expressão que mais usaria e explica quando.
Comparem equivalentes em duplas.
answers: Asking about a problem · Strong advice · Friendly suggestion · Personal view · Reacting
extra: Which one sounds like an order?

errors.w: If I was you, I go.
errors.r: If I were you, I’d go.

support: Trabalhe só as expressões ★ nesta aula.

patterns.name: Advice with should
ex: You should stop looking at your phone.
You shouldn’t drink coffee after four.
You should talk to your boss.

patterns.name: Suggestions
ex: Why don’t you turn off notifications?
Why don’t you take a walk after work?

patterns.name: Hypothetical advice
patterns.formula: **If I were you,** I’d + base verb
ex: If I were you, I’d talk to my boss.
If I were you, I’d go to bed earlier.

patterns.name: Soft options
ex: Maybe you could read before bed.
Maybe you could try a new routine.

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: Perhaps you could consider asking her.
If I were you, I’d go.
In your position, I would go.
register.note: Among friends, short and warm phrases are normal; in formal writing, recommend and consider are more common.

teach.goal: Fixar os padrões principais (01 e 02); os outros são expansão. Usar a troca de palavras para variar a fala.
solo: Mostre o padrão DENTRO do diálogo (grife os chunks).
Use “Swap the words”: toque em cada peça e peça que o estudante diga a frase completa.
Compare spoken × written em 2 exemplos.
group: Troca em cadeia: cada estudante muda UMA peça e o próximo repete a frase.
Em pares: um escolhe as peças, o outro fala.
teach.answers: Padrões 01 e 02 são o foco; 03 e 04 são expansão para quem avançar rápido.
extra: Give advice to a friend who is late every day.
Say one advice with each pattern.
support: Fique só com o padrão 01 na primeira rodada.
stretch: Combine dois padrões na mesma resposta.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: Should and could are weak in speech: /ʃəd/, /kəd/. The l is silent. Shouldn’t has two syllables: SHOULD-nt /ˈʃʊdnt/.

own.prompt: Write a piece of advice you would give a friend who cannot sleep.
own.criteria: Say it twice. Is should weak and the action stronger?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno de pronúncia: Reduction: should / shouldn’t / could.
solo: 3 passagens: escutar e identificar, reproduzir ritmo e entonação, usar em frase com conteúdo próprio.
Modele devagar e em velocidade normal; peça que bata palmas na sílaba forte.
group: Coro, depois duplas; circule ouvindo.
Cada estudante cria uma frase própria usando o fenômeno.
answers: Identify: You shouldn’t go. · Why don’t you try?
support: Reduza a velocidade e conte as batidas em voz alta.

levels.h: Controlled practice — choose the best answer

items.q: 1. A friend says: “I can’t sleep.” Best advice?
opts: You should stop drinking coffee after four.
You should to drink less coffee.
Why don’t you talk to your boss?
Why you don’t talk to boss?

items.q: 3. You want to say what you would do.
opts: If I were you, I’d call him.
If I am you, I’d call him.
If I would you, I call him.
items.why: If I were you, I’d + base verb.

items.q: 4. A friend gives you good advice. React.

levels.h: Guided practice — complete, substitute and transform

items.text: If I ___ you, I’d say sorry.

items.why: Why don’t you + base verb is a friendly suggestion.

ans: If I were you, I’d talk to my boss.
If I were you, I would talk to my boss.
If I were you, I’d talk to your boss.
items.model: If I were you, I’d talk to my boss.
items.why: If I were you, I’d + base verb.

items.npc: I’m so stressed about my exam.
opts: What’s going on? Why don’t you make a study plan?
items.why: Ask first, then offer a gentle suggestion.

teach.goal: Do controlado ao guiado: escolher, completar, substituir e responder antes da fala livre.
solo: Peça que o estudante justifique cada resposta.
Se acertar rápido, peça uma versão mais informal ou mais educada.
group: Resolvam em duplas e comparem antes de revelar.
Equipes: ponto por resposta justificada.
answers: You should stop drinking coffee after four. · Why don’t you talk to your boss? · If I were you, I’d call him. · That’s a good idea. Thanks! · shouldn’t · were · Why don’t you call her? · If I were you, I’d talk to my boss. · What’s going on? Why don’t you make a study plan?
extra: Say each correct sentence in a friendly voice.

errors.r: I’d advise you to drink water. / You should drink water.

support: Ofereça o banco de palavras (chips) nas lacunas.

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — a friend needs advice

brief.teacher: You are a friend with a small everyday problem. Reject one piece of advice and ask for another.
brief.student: You are the friend giving advice: ask questions, give advice and stay friendly.

orders: A friend who is nervous about a job interview
A friend who spends too much money
complications: The friend says “I already tried that”: offer something else.
The friend says “I don’t have time”: adapt the advice.
You don’t know the word for something: explain it differently.
The friend gets upset: use a softer form.
success: I give two pieces of advice.
I react to my friend’s answer.

teach.goal: Simulação com complicação inesperada e três rodadas com menos apoio.
solo: Combine o cenário com a vida real do estudante.
Rodada 1: com chunks. Rodada 2: só palavras-chave. Rodada 3: sem roteiro.
Meta de fala: 60–70% do tempo para o estudante. Anote 2–3 correções para a devolutiva.
extra: What if the friend does not want advice?

errors.w: You have to do this now!

support: Volte à rodada 1 se travar; peça que repita só a primeira frase.
stretch: Acrescente uma segunda complicação no meio da cena.

rounds.title: Listen and ask
rounds.task: Your partner shares a small problem. Ask two questions.
rounds.hint: What’s going on? / When did it start?

rounds.title: Give advice
rounds.task: Give two pieces of advice with different structures.

rounds.title: Not that
rounds.task: The advice does not work: explain and ask for another idea.
rounds.hint: I tried that, but… / Maybe you could…

rounds.title: Best advice
rounds.task: Whole group: each pair shares the best advice from their talk.
rounds.hint: We think… / If I were you…

infogap.title: Advice cards
infogap.instr: Ask your partner and complete your card. Do not look at the other card!

a.title: Problem and one tip
a.task: You know Ana’s problem and your tip. Ask for the second tip and the doctor’s advice.

b.title: Two tips
b.task: You know the second tip and the doctor’s advice. Ask about the problem and tip 1.

teach.goal: Fluência por repetição da função com informações novas a cada rodada.
group: Troque os pares a cada rodada (A+B / C+D → A+C / B+D → A+D / B+C → grupo todo).
Responsabilidade individual: cada aluno faz ≥1 pergunta e ≥1 resposta.
Circule anotando 2–3 correções prioritárias.
answers: A: headaches at night, drink more water. B: turn off screens early, sleep eight hours. Perguntas: What’s Ana’s problem? What should she do?
support: Entregue frases-modelo no chat da turma.

pages.title: Group mission — the advice hour
pages.goal: Each group must help a friend with a real small problem, using advice that sounds friendly.

missions.mission: One friend is stressed about a new job; the other asks questions and gives three pieces of advice.
missions.start: You look tired. What’s going on?

missions.mission: One roommate is always late; the other gives advice without sounding rude.
missions.constraint: Use “If I were you, I’d…” and “Maybe you could…”
missions.start: Can I give you some advice?

missions.mission: A student is nervous about a speaking test; the friend helps with a plan.
missions.constraint: Use “You shouldn’t…” and react with “That’s a good idea.”

success: I give two pieces of advice.
I react to my friend’s answer.

teach.goal: Realizar algo com o inglês: o objetivo é resolver, não só falar certo.
group: Cada grupo recebe papel, restrição e missão. Alterne os papéis.
Progressão: 1ª rodada com frases de apoio, 2ª só palavras-chave, 3ª sem roteiro.
Observe e anote 2–3 correções prioritárias; devolutiva no fim.
answers: Modelo: “What’s going on?” → “I can’t sleep.” → “You should stop looking at your phone.” → “That’s a good idea.”
support: Dê o início de frase (“Start with”) em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short message to a friend who has a problem. Show you care and give two pieces of advice.
pages.model: Hi Joe! I’m sorry you can’t sleep. **You should** stop looking at your phone before bed. **Why don’t you** turn off email notifications after nine? **If I were you,** I’d also talk to my boss. Let me know if you want to talk. Hang in there!
checklist: I gave a suggestion with Why don’t you…?
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea instead of rewriting everything.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à situação comunicativa.
solo: Peça o texto; corrija 2–3 pontos prioritários e mostre uma forma mais natural.
group: Cada estudante escreve; depois troquem os textos e corrijam em duplas.
support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

criteria.name: Fluency
criteria.desc: Mantém a comunicação sem interrupções excessivas.

criteria.name: Language use
criteria.desc: Utiliza adequadamente padrões, vocabulário e expressões.

criteria.name: Pronunciation
criteria.desc: É compreensível e usa ritmo e entonação adequados.

criteria.name: Interaction
criteria.desc: Responde, pergunta, esclarece e desenvolve a conversa.

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.
Functional performance. Work on the lowest criteria in the next lesson.
Good control. Raise complexity and speed; add follow-up questions.
Strong performance. Move to a more demanding situation.

prompts.well: Example: You asked a question before giving advice and sounded friendly.
prompts.improve: Example: After should, use the base verb (You should go, not You should to go).
prompts.next: Example: Give advice to two friends with different problems.

teach.goal: Avaliar o que o aluno conseguiu comunicar, não só os erros gramaticais.
solo: O estudante se autoavalia primeiro; depois você.
Feche com os três blocos: What you did well · What to improve · Your next challenge.
group: Dê um comentário por critério a cada estudante.
Cada um escolhe o próprio próximo desafio.
teach.answers: A rubrica é uma ferramenta interna de acompanhamento, não uma certificação CEFR.

tasks.name: Build a question
tasks.prompt: Without notes: ask a friend what is wrong.

tasks.name: Respond to a situation
tasks.prompt: A friend says: “I never exercise.” Give advice.
tasks.model: You should take a short walk every day.

tasks.name: Use a new expression
tasks.prompt: Say what you would do in your friend’s place.
tasks.model: If I were you, I’d talk to my boss.

items: Record a 45–60 second audio giving advice to a friend.
Write a message with three pieces of advice, using three different structures.
Collect five problems and write one friendly suggestion for each.
Listen to the dialogue again and notice how Mina softens her advice.

unit: Tell · describe · compare · book · opine · advise · plan

teach.goal: Toda aula termina com uma produção observável.
solo: Sem consultar as anotações: construir uma pergunta, responder a uma situação e usar uma expressão nova.
group: Exit challenge individual; compare com o colega e combine a tarefa de continuidade.
answers: What’s going on? · You should take a short walk every day. · If I were you, I’d talk to my boss.
extra: Revisão espaçada: retomar conselhos na aula 78 (missão integrada).

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.say: You should stop using your phone before bed. Why don’t you read a book?
ladder.goal: Give friendly advice in different ways.

ladder.say: If I were you, I’d talk to your manager about the hours, because it’s affecting your health.
It might be worth setting clear boundaries, as otherwise you’ll end up exhausted.
I’d seriously consider renegotiating the terms, since the current arrangement doesn’t seem sustainable.
One might gently suggest that the job should serve the life, not the other way round.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
solo: Mostre onde o estudante está e a próxima etapa.
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do próprio nível e a do próximo.
extra: Which sentence would you like to be able to say next month?
